pairs.question: Quid ergo amplius est Iudaeo aut quae utilitas circumcisionis?
pairs.answer: Multum per omnem modum primum quidem quia credita sunt illis eloquia Dei.
pairs.derivation: Paul poses a double rhetorical question (v.1) and answers it himself in v.2. Answer kept whole through the explanatory 'quia' clause that constitutes the actual reply; nothing cut. Verse-number scaffolding stripped, capitalization and terminal punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Quid ergo dicemus? Permanebimus in peccato ut gratia abundet?
pairs.derivation: Classic diatribe: rhetorical question (v.1) emphatically answered by Paul's own 'absit' which opens v.2. Answer cut at 'absit' (first full stop); what follows ('qui enim mortui sumus peccato quomodo adhuc vivemus in illo') is elaboration/justification, not the direct answer. Scaffolding stripped, punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Quid ergo? Peccavimus quoniam non sumus sub lege sed sub gratia?
pairs.derivation: Rhetorical question and Paul's own 'absit' answer occur within v.15. Answer ends at 'absit'; the following 'nescitis quoniam...' (v.16) is subsequent argument, not the direct reply. Scaffolding stripped, capitalization/punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Quid ergo dicemus? Lex peccatum est?
pairs.derivation: Rhetorical question and immediate 'absit' answer both in v.7. Cut after 'absit'; the continuation 'sed peccatum non cognovi nisi per legem...' is qualification/elaboration, not the direct answer. Scaffolding stripped, punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Infelix ego homo, quis me liberabit de corpore mortis huius?
pairs.answer: Gratia Dei per Iesum Christum Dominum nostrum.
pairs.derivation: v.24 question; setup 'Infelix ego homo' kept verbatim so the cry has its context. Answer is the opening nominal phrase of v.25; cut before 'igitur ego ipse mente servio...' which turns to summary reflection rather than answering 'who will deliver me'. Scaffolding stripped, punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Quid ergo dicemus? Numquid iniquitas apud Deum?
pairs.derivation: Rhetorical question with 'numquid' answered by Paul's own 'absit', all within v.14. Cut at 'absit'; the following 'Mosi enim dicit...' (v.15) is scriptural support, not the direct answer. Scaffolding stripped, punctuation normalized.

pairs.question: Numquid reppulit Deus populum suum?
pairs.answer: Absit, nam et ego Israhelita sum ex semine Abraham tribu Beniamin.
pairs.derivation: v.1 question with 'numquid' answered by Paul's own 'absit'; the 'nam' clause giving himself as living proof is the operative completion of the one-sentence answer, so kept. Cut before v.2 'non reppulit Deus plebem suam...'. The preceding 'dico ergo' (speech framing) dropped. Scaffolding stripped, punctuation normalized.
